learning_outcomes.text: To understand the mechanisms and modes of heat transfer and to identify the corresponding governing fundamental equations.
To comprehend the physical phenomena and their modelling through simplified mathematical models.
To provide a first contact with heat transfer experimental techniques.
To be able to perform qualitative and quantitative analyses in cases where relatively simple analytical solutions or simplified correlations exist.
To use quantitative analysis tools in design situations, through the use of supporting calculation means.
Ability to understand and interpret the phenomena involving heat transfer processes.
Ability to develop quantitative analysis of processes, though analytical methods involving experimental correlations.
Being able to apply the knowledge in the analysis and design of equipment, regarding temperature distributions and heat fluxes.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to Heat Transfer mechanisms and modes: difference between the Heat Transfer and the Thermodynamics approaches; simple cases of conduction, convection and radiation; notion of thermal resistance.

Conduction: Fourier equation; thermal conductivity and diffusivity; general conduction equation; steady unidimensional conduction (plane wall, cylinder and sphere, without and with internal generation, fins); brief introduction to numerical solutions for multidimensional steady conduction; transient conduction (global system, unidimensional analytical solutions for plane wall, cylinder and sphere).

Convection: energy equation for fluid flow; dimensionless numbers; convection coefficient; internal and external flows and their correlations; natural convection in simple geometries (plate, cylinder, rectangular cavity) and correlations.
Phase change: film condensation outside plane walls and tubes, and their correlations; pool boiling: regimes and correlations.

Radiation: electromagnetic and thermal radiation; fundamental concepts; black body and its properties; radiative properties of materials; radiation exchanges in a non-participating media (radiosity, view factor and balances); combined radiation and convection; radiation shields; electrical analogy and its limitations.
Heat exchangers: types and geometry; mean log temperature difference and efficiency; efficiency-NTU relationships for different geometries.
teaching_methods: Theoretical-practical sessions to explain concepts and equations and analyze practical examples
Weekly session to assist in the solution of practical problems
Laboratory practice with 2 group works followed by a questionnaire
assessment_rules: Normal distributed evaluation consists of laboratory works (10%), an intermediate test (40%), and a final exam (50% or 90% if overrunning the intermediate test). Recurso/RUN-UP and special exams are 100% based on the final exam. All duly registered students with over 75% registered attendance are admitted to exams. Classification improvement is possible via a Recurso exam.
